title: Microsoft Purview: diagnostics that explain DLP and auto-labeling results for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange
summary: Hold: reviewing Purview role group membership alone does not establish who can run the diagnostics, because Microsoft Entra role assignments also grant access. The auto-labeling progress command is not documented as returning file failures; its scope needs to be distinguished from the portal failure list.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details reaches the auto-labeling failure view.
claims.quote: Select Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... select View details in the policy details panel. ... Select Labeling failures to see failed label applications, or Label removal failures for a policy that removes labels.
claims.fix: For label-application failures, extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details > Labeling failures'. In the After rollout bullet, replace 'the policy's View details failure list' with 'the policy's View details > Labeling failures list'. The cited page also documents Label removal failures for removal policies.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback provides labeling failure results for the policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy IncludeProgressFeedback labeling failures report. Opened get-autosensitivitylabelpolicy, apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, and auto-labeling-failures-sharepoint-onedrive. The command reference documents progress counts, not file-failure results.
claims.fix: Keep the command, but qualify controls[3].note and its rendered table note: 'The portal shows file failures. The cmdlet reports labeling progress only: files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled policies; file-failure details are not documented for this switch. Cmdlet is in Security & Compliance PowerShell.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/get-autosensitivitylabelpolicy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Purview role group membership is the deciding control for who holds the roles that allow diagnostic access.
claims.quote: If you assign both an Entra role and a scoped Microsoft Purview role group assignment to a user or group ... the Entra role takes precedence at runtime. As a result, the user's effective permissions are unscoped
claims.fix: Replace 'Role group membership (first row of the controls table) decides who that is' with 'Purview role group membership is one route to these permissions; Microsoft Entra assignments of the listed roles also grant access.' Replace 'Access to the diagnostics follows from the roles each set requires, so role group membership is the deciding control' with 'Access to the diagnostics follows from the roles each set requires; review both Purview role group membership and Microsoft Entra assignments of those roles.' The existing cited permissions page documents the Entra mappings and precedence.
